kurz: When reducing, water evaporates. Flavour, salt and gelatine stay behind and become more concentrated.
bild_im_kopf: Like a closing-down sale in a shop: the shelves empty (water), but the best pieces (flavour) stay and stand out all the more.
was_passiert: If you boil a liquid uncovered, mainly water evaporates. Everything else stays in the pot: aromas, sugar, salt and, in stocks, the gelatine from the bones. That is why a jus turns stronger and silkier as it reduces, without any flour or starch.
warum_wichtig: Gives sauces depth and natural body. But salt concentrates too: salt at the start and you end up with an oversalted sauce.
faustregeln: Salt only at the end: [[reduzieren|reducing]] concentrates the salt too.
Wide pot or pan: more surface, faster reduction.
A stock with lots of gelatine thickens by itself as it reduces.

praxis.text: Red wine sauce: reduce wine and stock to a third, then [[montieren|mount]] with cold butter.
Reducing fruit juice to a syrup concentrates sugar and acid.
